title: Antigen retrieval by citrate solution improves western blot signal
author: Patiño-García, Rocha-Pérez, et al.
materials: Testes of C57BL/6J mice and human endometriotic cells lines (Hs 832 and 11Z) were used for this study. Protein extraction was performed as previously published [9]. Briefly, the homogenization of both testes and cells was performed in a radio immunoprecipitation assay buffer (RIPA), with a protease inhibitor cocktail (Sigma) and a phosphatase inhibitor cocktail with 2 mM 4-(2-aminoethyl) benzenesulfonyl fluoride hydrochloride, 0.3 μM aprotinin, 130 μM bestatin hydrochloride, 14 μM E-64, 1 mM EDTA, and 1 μM leupeptinhemisulfate. Proteins were purified by centrifugation at 12,000 × g at 4 °C for 10 min and subsequently quantified by Bradford method.

steps.title: Prepare RIPA lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Make radio immunoprecipitation assay (RIPA) buffer and add a protease inhibitor cocktail (Sigma) and a phosphatase inhibitor cocktail containing 2 mM 4-(2-aminoethyl)benzenesulfonyl fluoride hydrochloride, 0.3 µM aprotinin, 130 µM bestatin hydrochloride, 14 µM E‑64, 1 mM EDTA, and 1 µM leupeptin hemisulfate.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue and cells
steps.instruction: Homogenize testes of C57BL/6J mice and the human endometriotic cell lines Hs832 and 11Z in the prepared RIPA buffer.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysates
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenates at 12,000 × g, 4 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Quantify protein concentration
steps.instruction: Determine the protein concentration of the cleared supernatant using the Bradford assay.

steps.title: Perform antigen retrieval
steps.instruction: Incubate the protein samples in sodium citrate buffer on a water bath (heat‑induced epitope retrieval) as described in the study.
